note: Early studies reported corpus callosum hypoplasia consistently in recurrent missense cases, but newer cohorts with over 34% loss-of-function variants observe corpus callosum thinning in 62.1% of patients.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 32 individuals with MAPK8IP3 variants comprising missense (62.5%) and predicted loss-of-function variants (34.4%), corpus callosum thinning was reported in 62.1%.

source.title: Comprehensive Clinical Characteristics, Longitudinal Adaptive Functioning, and Electroencephalogram Activity in MAPK8IP3‐Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder
source.quote: Corpus callosum thinning was reported in 62.1%.

evidence.text: Initial reports observed that brain anomalies such as hypoplasia of the corpus callosum were consistent among individuals harboring recurrent de novo missense variants in MAPK8IP3.

source.title: De novo variants in MAPK8IP3 cause intellectual disability with variable brain anomalies
source.quote: Brain anomalies such as perisylvian polymicrogyria, cerebral or cerebellar atrophy, and hypoplasia of the corpus callosum were consistent among individuals harboring recurrent de novo missense variants.
